alternatives.argument: Define the index from finite-dimensional cohomology representations and their alternating character; use BGV Chapter 6 §6.1 for the compact-group representation-ring convention and Zelin Yi §1 for the elliptic-complex cohomology setup.

For first-order elliptic complexes and simple isolated fixed points, use Zelin Yi Theorem 1.1 and §§2–5: the heat supertrace is invariant in t, relative tangent-groupoid rescaling reduces it to the constant-symbol heat kernel at each fixed point, Fourier inversion gives unit tangent integral, and change of variables contributes the absolute Jacobian denominator.

sources.title: Zelin Yi, A Groupoid Proof of the Lefschetz fixed point formula
sources.locator: Complete 11-page paper retrieved. §1, PDF pp. 1–2: first-order elliptic complexes, simple fixed points and Theorem 1.1. §§2–4, pp. 2–8: relative tangent groupoid, rescaled heat-kernel family and coefficient bundle. §5, pp. 8–10: fixed-point supertrace calculation, unit integral of the constant-symbol heat kernel, and the absolute Jacobian denominator.

contents.name: §1 and Theorem 1.1: equivariant Lefschetz formula for first-order elliptic complexes
contents.support: The source states the compact-manifold theorem for an order-one elliptic complex, a commuting lifted smooth map, and simple fixed points; it identifies the cohomological alternating trace with the fixed-point sum.

contents.name: §§2–4: relative tangent-groupoid heat-kernel extension and rescaled local family
contents.support: The paper constructs the groupoid-rescaled heat-kernel family and identifies its constant-symbol tangent kernel; the batch lemma states this input exactly and records the missing local proof carrier.

contents.name: §§2–5: relative tangent-groupoid proof
contents.support: The proof constructs the rescaled family, identifies its t=0 constant-symbol heat kernel, applies Fourier inversion to show its tangent integral is one, and changes variables by the invertible fixed-point derivative to obtain the absolute determinant denominator.

sources.title: Nicole Berline, Ezra Getzler, and Michèle Vergne, Heat Kernels and Dirac Operators
sources.locator: Complete book text retrieved. Chapter 2 §§2.4–2.7, printed pp. 77–100: heat-kernel parametrix, Gaussian remainder estimates, and smooth parameter dependence. Chapter 6 §6.2, printed pp. 187–190: Atiyah–Bott formula for isolated fixed points and Lemma 6.4 local heat-kernel concentration for complexes with Dirac-type Hodge operator. §§6.3–6.4 and §6.7, printed pp. 191–197 and 203–205: equivariant Dirac fixed-component formula and its local heat-kernel proof.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.1: equivariant Dirac index as a representation-ring character
contents.support: Chapter 6 §6.1 identifies the finite-dimensional graded kernel representation and its virtual character in R(G). The authored definition extends that construction to bounded equivariant elliptic complexes with finite-dimensional cohomology.

contents.name: Chapter 2 §§2.4–2.7 and Chapter 6 §6.2, Lemma 6.4: parametrix and isolated-point kernel concentration
contents.support: The book constructs parameter-dependent generalized-Laplacian heat kernels and proves local concentration for isolated points in the Dirac-type-complex case. This supports the analytic route, but the batch has not locally reproduced these estimates for its full general elliptic-complex scope.

contents.name: Chapter 6 §6.2, §§6.3–6.4 and §6.7: isolated Atiyah–Bott formula and Dirac fixed-component formula
contents.support: Section 6.2 states the isolated elliptic-complex formula and proves its Dirac-type-complex case using Lemma 6.4; §§6.3–6.4 and §6.7 treat the distinct positive-dimensional fixed-component Dirac formula. The Dirac-type hypothesis is narrower than the authored general first-order complex.

sources.title: J. L. Heitsch, The Lefschetz Principle, Fixed Point Theory, and Index Theory
sources.locator: Complete 13-page lecture note. §3, PDF pp. 8–9: Theorem 3.1 states the general elliptic-complex fixed-point formula; the proof derives the cohomological heat-trace identity and localizes the kernel near the fixed set, but leaves the final local calculation abbreviated. Used as an independent statement/heat-route treatment, not as the complete local Jacobian proof.

contents.name: §3 setup: cohomological Lefschetz number and geometric endomorphism of an elliptic complex
contents.support: The notes define the alternating trace of the induced maps on finite-dimensional elliptic-complex cohomology and the bundle-map lift over a smooth self-map.

contents.name: Theorem 3.1: Atiyah–Bott fixed-point formula for elliptic complexes
contents.support: The statement gives the alternating fiber trace divided by the absolute determinant for transverse graph/diagonal intersection. The exact simple-fixed-point specialization is used for the authored theorem.

contents.name: §3 proof of Theorem 3.1: spectral heat trace and local Gaussian concentration
contents.support: The proof derives heat-trace invariance and concentration near fixed points, but explicitly leaves the last local calculation as a direct computation; it does not supply the batch lemma’s rescaled-kernel domination proof.
